```rust
/// The certificate the port serves: over the identity's key, naming
/// where a browser reaches the host. Reissued only when `names` or
/// `address` no longer match or `not_after` is near.
pub struct ServedCertificate {
    /// DER, base64.
    pub certificate: String,
    /// The SANs it carries, in order.
    pub names: Vec<String>,
    /// The routed address among them, which the QR uses.
    pub address: Option<IpAddr>,
    pub not_after: SystemTime,
}
```

`certificate` in `Identity` stays as it is (the identity's own record
and what `make_identity` checks against the key); `tls_config` serves
`served` when present. A key rotation makes a new identity with
`served: None`. An older build reads the file and ignores the field
(`Identity` has no `deny_unknown_fields`); if it saves the identity, the
field is dropped and the next newer launch issues a fresh leaf, which a
browser meets as one more warning. The struct literals of `Identity`
gain `served: None` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:117`,
`src/core/tests.rs:11769`, `tests/ui.rs:7436`).

Rehydration: at bind the app compares `served` with the names it would
issue now and its expiry; a match is served as it is, anything else is
reissued and saved (The actions and effects). Nothing else new is
rehydrated.

1	# Plan for #230: the browser page on the remote port
2	
3	Worktree at 7fe8949. Line references are to this tree. `SCHEMA_VERSION`
4	is 16 (`src/core/model.rs:12`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1
5	(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). Neither moves: the one serialized change is
6	an additive `#[serde(default)]` field on `Identity`, the way `listen`
7	was added under version 1 (`src/ports/remote.rs:39-40`); see The
8	record. "Facts" is `facts/1/repo/facts.md`.
9	
10	## Where this departs from the issue
11	
12	- **The code travels in the fragment, not the query.** The QR is
13	  `https://<addr>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
14	  A browser never sends a fragment to the server, so the code never
15	  reaches a request target, `RemoteRequest::query` or a `Referer`. It
16	  reaches the host only in the `/pair` body. That makes the notes'
17	  questions about logging the query, refusing a `GET /?code=`, and
18	  `Referer` leakage go away. This rests on RFC 3986 §3.5 (the user agent
19	  handles the fragment). That is not in the facts file, and
20	  `tests/remote.rs` cannot show it, because the host's client is not a
21	  browser. The page still calls `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`
22	  before anything else, but facts list whether Safari or the camera
23	  records the URL first as Unresolved (facts:46). The fragment does not
24	  change that, and the plan accepts it: the code is single-use, and the
25	  window closes on the first pairing (`src/core/remote.rs:64`).
26	- **The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire.** `agent_excerpt`
27	  derives it in the UI from the parsed conversation (facts:17,
28	  `src/ui/cards.rs:558-574`), and `SessionView` has no such field
29	  (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`). The page's list shows
30	  `waiting_reason` when the session is waiting, otherwise the card word
31	  (`card`), plus the first line of `notes`. Facts leave the excerpt to
32	  the owner (facts:83). If the owner wants it, the fallback is an
33	  additive `#[serde(default)] excerpt: Option<String>` on `SessionView`,
34	  computed on the host by the `agent_excerpt` rule. That means a
35	  fixture rewrite and a `revision.rs` fingerprint change, so it is a
36	  separate commit.
37	- **The current certificate is not one a phone is sure to accept.** It
38	  has no SAN, validity to 4096, and no serverAuth EKU (facts:13, :33).
39	  The host issues a second, served leaf over the same Keychain key,
40	  keeps it in `identity.json`, and reissues it only when its names no
41	  longer match or its expiry is within 30 days (details under The
42	  record and The signals). Pins survive (facts:12, spec §5 "a
43	  certificate reissued from the same key"). A browser's acceptance of
44	  the served leaf survives an app restart, because the leaf is the same
45	  bytes. Each issue has its own random serial, so no two certificates
46	  share issuer and serial (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.2; rcgen would otherwise
47	  derive the serial from the key, `rcgen-0.14.10/src/certificate.rs:458-468`).
48	- **"Revoked" is told apart by the page, not the host.** A revoked
49	  token and an unknown token get the same 401 (`src/app.rs:3142-3148`).
50	  The page keeps `{server_id, spki_sha256}` per origin in
51	  `localStorage`. On a 401 it says "revoked" when `/info` still shows
52	  that key, "identity changed, pair again" when the key differs, and
53	  "not paired" when it kept nothing. Facts leave this to the owner
54	  (facts:91). If the owner says otherwise, the fallback is a distinct
55	  401 code, which needs a record of revoked token hashes. Safari wipes
56	  script storage after 7 days without a visit (facts:32), so after that
57	  a revoked browser hears "not paired, scan the QR". That is still the
58	  right instruction.
59	- **"The screen for anything else" has no screen when the session is
60	  stopped.** `screen` refuses a session that is not running (spec
61	  §4.3). The page says "Not running; nothing to show". Facts leave this
62	  to the owner (facts:94). If the owner wants more, the fallback is
63	  `runs` then `runs/{n}/output` for a command or service.
64	- **The cookie is not scoped by port** (facts:28). A cookie set by
65	  `https://<ip>:43187` is sent to every port on that address. So the
66	  cookie name carries the port. Every cookie-authenticated request also
67	  passes an origin check, because `SameSite=Strict` does not stop
68	  another HTTPS service on the same IP: that service is same-site.
69	
70	## Decisions
71	
72	1. **Trust: the click-through is the trust step, and a browser pairs
73	   `read` only.** This is the owner's decision (facts:56-58), not a
74	   settled line, and it weakens two guarantees of §5:
75	   - "Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent"
76	     (`docs/remote-client.md:309`). A browser cannot. An impostor that
77	     the owner clicks through serves its own page, reads the fragment
78	     and relays the code with the real key. The URL's `key` then only
79	     catches a QR for another host or a stale QR: a genuine page
80	     compares it with `/info`'s self-reported `spki_sha256` and posts
81	     nothing on a mismatch.
82	   - "after pairing, every connection verifies the pin before the token
83	     is presented" (same line), and the token "is sent only as a bearer
84	     header over the pinned connection" (`:312`). A browser sends its
85	     cookie to whatever certificate it has accepted for the origin.
86	
87	   What the plan builds against that: a stable served leaf (The
88	   record), so a second warning on a known origin is
89	   a sign of trouble rather than routine; and **a browser pairing is
90	   granted `read` whatever the window's scope.** The owner raises it to
91	   `control` by hand in the devices dialog, which §5 already allows
92	   (`docs/remote-client.md:314`). A relayed code therefore yields a
93	   reader, never a device that types into agent sessions, unless the
94	   owner raises it. The host tells a browser pairing by the `/pair`
95	   body's `"cookie": true` (decision 2). The dialog says what the
96	   click-through trusts in one sentence, and the hover on a browser's
97	   scope combo says what raising it trusts.
98	
99	   §5's lines 309, 312 and 317 are rewritten to say the native
100	   guarantee and the browser's weaker one side by side, not added to
101	   (Docs).
102	
103	   **If the owner rejects the click-through as the trust step**, the
104	   fallback the implementer builds is facts:58: the host serves its
105	   certificate before pairing at `GET /certificate`
106	   (`application/x-x509-ca-cert`), issued with basicConstraints CA:TRUE
107	   plus the served leaf's SAN, EKU and ≤825-day validity (facts:33,
108	   :34). The dialog gives the Settings > General > About > Certificate
109	   Trust Settings steps (facts:34), the pre-pairing rule names a fourth
110	   path, and browsers keep the window's scope. Without that answer the
111	   build is the read cap above.
112	
113	   Separately, whether iOS Safari opens `wss://` after the click-through
114	   is Unresolved (facts:38, owner item facts:53). **The build does not
115	   depend on that answer.** The page falls back on its own to polling
116	   REST every 5 s when the socket fails before `hello`. Spike 23
117	   records it (Tests).
118	2. **Token: an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` cookie, no
119	   `Domain`, `Max-Age=34560000`.** The page's script never sees it. It
120	   survives Safari's 7-day storage cap where `localStorage` does not
121	   (facts:32). The same-origin WebSocket handshake sends it (facts:25).
122	   Name: `switchboard-<port>`, so two instances on one Mac never
123	   overwrite each other's cookie (facts:28). Native clients keep the
124	   bearer header, which is checked first. The page calls `fetch` in its
125	   default mode (`cors`) and never sets `mode` or `referrerPolicy` on a
126	   request: under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, a non-GET request in
127	   any other mode carries `Origin: null` (Fetch, "append a request
128	   `Origin` header" step 4.1), which the origin rule refuses. Whether a page reached through
129	   a certificate override is a secure context, and so keeps a `Secure`
130	   cookie, is Unresolved (facts:45). If Safari drops the cookie, the
131	   fallback is the subprotocol route: `/pair` returns the token in the
132	   body, the page keeps it in `localStorage`, sends it as
133	   `Authorization` on `fetch` and as the offered `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`,
134	   and `respond_upgrade` echoes it (facts:18, :26, :27). Re-pairing
135	   after 7 days unused is the known cost.
136	3. **One QR: the URL.** The JSON form leaves the QR and "Copy invite".
137	   `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
138	   accepts the URL and still accepts the JSON, because
139	   `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` lines and older pasted invites are JSON. That
140	   one function covers every caller (facts:14). The URL carries one
141	   address: the routed address the served leaf names
142	   (`ServedCertificate::address`, The record), bracketed when it is
143	   IPv6, so the QR's host and the certificate's SAN cannot disagree.
144	   When the pairing window opens and `local_address()` differs from
145	   that address (the Mac changed networks since the bind), the app
146	   reissues the leaf and rebinds before the QR is drawn (The actions
147	   and effects). The dialog already shows only one address. Facts leave which
148	   address to the owner (facts:71). If the owner says otherwise, the
149	   fallback is a `.local` name, which is Unresolved (facts:49) and not
150	   built.
151	4. **Static paths.** `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
152	   `GET /app.js` (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.css`
153	   (`text/css; charset=utf-8`). Nothing else: `/index.html`,
154	   `/favicon.ico` and every other non-API path answer 404 `not_found`
155	   as today. Each of the three carries `Content-Security-Policy:
156	   default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src
157	   'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none';
158	   frame-ancestors 'none'` as a header. `connect-src 'self'` covers the
159	   same-origin `wss:` (facts:30), and `frame-ancestors` must be a
160	   header (facts:31). They also carry `Cache-Control: no-store`,
161	   `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
162	   Every JSON reply also gains `Cache-Control: no-store` and `nosniff`.
163	   A static request **without** a `switchboard-<port>` cookie is
164	   answered by the connection thread, without the frame, the way it
165	   answers 429: the bytes are compile-time constants with nothing of
166	   the host in them. A static request **with** that cookie goes to the
167	   frame, which serves the same bytes and answers `authenticated: true`
168	   when the cookie is a known token (`device_by_token`, no
169	   `DeviceSeen`, no origin rule: a GET of public bytes has no effect).
170	   The connection then moves to the paired pool as an API request's
171	   does (`src/adapters/remote.rs:834-848`). Without this, a paired
172	   phone's reload leaves connections that fetched only `/app.css` in the
173	   unauthenticated pool for the 30 s idle timeout (`:573`, set at
174	   `:785`), and the accept loop drops a fifth (`:701-706`): the phone's
175	   own `/device` and anyone's `/info` would be locked out for 30 s. An
176	   unknown cookie still gets the page, unauthenticated. Facts leave the
177	   thread to the owner (facts:74); the fallback is answering every
178	   static request in `serve_remote` before the `/api/v1/` strip. Static
179	   loads count in a new `page` window of 60 a minute per listener,
180	   shared by the three paths. How many connections iOS Safari opens at
181	   once is Unresolved (facts:48). An unpaired load is three files and
182	   `/info`, so at most four in the stranger pool, each held up to 30 s
183	   idle. Spike 23 counts them; if an unpaired load or a pairing right
184	   after it is dropped, the fallback is `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` 4 → 8 and
185	   the §4.1 line with it. §5's rule becomes: before pairing,
186	   nothing but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's three files, which carry
187	   nothing of the host. With neither a fragment nor a cookie, the page
188	   shows `/info`'s `server_name`, whether pairing is open, and "On the
189	   Mac, open Remote devices, allow pairing and scan the QR" (the owner
190	   question at facts:77; the fallback is static text alone).
191	5. **Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/index.html`,
192	   `web/app.js` and `web/app.css` are embedded with `include_str!`
193	   (the precedent for embedding is `include_bytes!` at
194	   `src/main.rs:167`; the tree has no `include_str!` yet). The test checks a fixed list
195	   of referenced paths. There is no HTML parser (facts:21) and no JS
196	   test harness, since the page has no build step and no dependency.
197	6. **Device record.** The page sends `device_name` from
198	   `navigator.userAgent`: "Safari on iPhone", "Safari on Mac", "Chrome
199	   on Android", and so on, else "Browser". Safari on iPadOS sends the
200	   Mac user agent by default
201	   (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/119186), so a Mac user
202	   agent with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1` is named "Safari on iPad".
203	   A heuristic: a Mac with a touch screen would read as an iPad, and
204	   the owner sees the name only in the devices list.
205	   `/pair` already takes it (`src/app.rs:3650`) and caps it at 64
206	   characters (`src/core/remote.rs:166`). Scope is `read` for a browser
207	   whatever the window says (decision 1). The device is listed and revocable as any other. There is no
208	   `kind` field; the name tells devices apart. Facts leave this to the
209	   owner (facts:80). If the owner wants one, the fallback is an additive
210	   `#[serde(default)] kind` on `PairedDevice`, with no version
211	   (facts:16).
212	7. **The page's scope after a reload: `GET /api/v1/device`.** It
213	   answers `{device_id, name, scope}` under any scope. The page cannot
214	   do without it: the cookie is unreadable, and storage is wiped after
215	   7 days. It is also the request the page uses to learn it was
216	   revoked. Facts leave this to the owner (facts:87). If the owner says
217	   no, the fallback is to keep the scope from the `/pair` reply in
218	   `localStorage`, show the reply box when the scope is unknown, and
219	   hide it on a `403 scope`.
220	8. **The cookie reaches every endpoint the bearer does.** There is no
221	   second allowlist, because scope is the authority and a browser is a
222	   paired device like any other. Facts leave this to the owner
223	   (facts:65). If the owner says otherwise, the fallback is a match on
224	   how the request authenticated, limited to the page's paths.
225	9. **`/info` lists a `web` capability.** It is additive: the Swift
226	   client checks `capabilities.contains(..)` (for example
227	   `client/Sources/SwitchboardClientCore/ServerConnection.swift:431`),
228	   so an unknown word is ignored.
229	
230	## The record
231	
232	`devices.json`: no change. A browser is a `PairedDevice`; the token's
233	hash is the same whether the token travels as a bearer header or as a
234	cookie.
235	
236	`identity.json` gains the served leaf, so a browser's acceptance
237	survives a restart. `Identity` (`src/ports/remote.rs:26`) gets an
238	additive `#[serde(default)] pub served: Option<ServedCertificate>`,
239	under `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged, as `listen` was
240	(`:39-40`). It is a field of the existing file rather than a new one
241	because it is written through the same `Effect::SaveIdentity` and
242	`RemoteStore::save_identity` path, so no port method is added.
243	
244	```rust
245	/// The certificate the port serves: over the identity's key, naming
246	/// where a browser reaches the host. Reissued only when `names` or
247	/// `address` no longer match or `not_after` is near.
248	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
249	pub struct ServedCertificate {
250	    /// DER, base64.
251	    pub certificate: String,
252	    /// The SANs it carries, in order.
253	    pub names: Vec<String>,
254	    /// The routed address among them, which the QR uses.
255	    pub address: Option<IpAddr>,
256	    pub not_after: SystemTime,
257	}
258	```
259	
260	`certificate` in `Identity` stays as it is (the identity's own record
261	and what `make_identity` checks against the key); `tls_config` serves
262	`served` when present. A key rotation makes a new identity with
263	`served: None`. An older build reads the file and ignores the field
264	(`Identity` has no `deny_unknown_fields`); if it saves the identity, the
265	field is dropped and the next newer launch issues a fresh leaf, which a
266	browser meets as one more warning. The struct literals of `Identity`
267	gain `served: None` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:117`,
268	`src/core/tests.rs:11769`, `tests/ui.rs:7436`).
269	
270	Rehydration: at bind the app compares `served` with the names it would
271	issue now and its expiry; a match is served as it is, anything else is
272	reissued and saved (The actions and effects). Nothing else new is
273	rehydrated. A browser's only state is its cookie and the
274	`{server_id, spki_sha256}` it keeps in storage for that origin. A
275	change of the Mac's address is a new origin, so the browser pairs again
276	from a fresh QR. Write that under Known gaps.
277	
278	## The signals
279	
280	These change in `src/adapters/remote.rs`.
281	
282	- `read_request` (:444) keeps three more headers on `RemoteRequest`
283	  (:360). `cookie: Option<String>` is only the value of the cookie
284	  named `switchboard-<port>`; other cookies are dropped. `origin:
285	  Option<String>` and `host: Option<String>` are the raw values.
286	  `page: bool` is true when `X-Switchboard-Page: 1` is present. The
287	  adapter learns its port from `Shared`, which gains `port: u16`,
288	  filled from `listener.local_addr()` in `bind` (:673).
289	- `connection` (:770) answers the three static paths itself when the
290	  request has no `cookie`, after the rate check, which gains the `page`
291	  window in `Limits::limited` (:629). With a cookie it hands them to
292	  the frame like any request (decision 4).
293	- `respond` (:530) takes a content type and extra header lines.
294	  `RemoteReply` (:389) gains `cookie: Option<String>`, the token to set
295	  as `Set-Cookie`. The existing constructors gain `cookie: None`.
296	- **The served leaf.** A new `pub fn serving_certificate(identity,
297	  key_pem, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime) ->
298	  Result<ServedCertificate, String>` makes the leaf over the Keychain
299	  key with `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem` (facts:12). It keeps the CN of
300	  `make_identity`. The SANs are `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the
301	  routed address; rcgen turns an IP string into `SanType::IpAddress`
302	  (facts:13). It sets `extended_key_usages = [ServerAuth]`,
303	  `not_before = now − 1 day`, `not_after = now + 800 days` (under
304	  Apple's 825, facts:33), and `serial_number =
305	  Some(SerialNumber::from_slice(&r))` with `r` 16 bytes from
306	  `fill_random` and the top bit cleared so the integer is positive
307	  (`rcgen-0.14.10/src/lib.rs:878`). `time` is already in the tree at
308	  0.3.55 behind rcgen. Add it as a direct dependency (`time = "0.3"`)
309	  for `OffsetDateTime::from(SystemTime)`, and commit the updated
310	  `Cargo.lock`.
311	- `tls_config` (:144) serves `identity.served` when it is present and
312	  `identity.certificate` otherwise. Its signature does not change.
313	- The rule for when to reissue is a pure function in
314	  `src/core/remote.rs`: `pub fn served_is_current(served:
315	  Option<&ServedCertificate>, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime)
316	  -> bool`, true when `served` exists, names `address`, and expires more
317	  than 30 days after `now`. If the owner answers "no" on naming the IP
318	  (facts:59), the SANs drop the routed address and `address` is not
319	  compared; the QR then takes `local_address()` itself.
320	
321	## The actions and effects
322	
323	One new action, `AppAction::ServedCertificateMade(ServedCertificate)`:
324	the core stores it on the identity through `update_identity`
325	(`src/core/remote.rs:105`), which emits the existing
326	`Effect::SaveIdentity`. No new `Effect`. `Paired` and `RevokeDevice`
327	carry a browser unchanged. The frame changes in `src/app.rs`:
328	
329	- `bind_remote` (:2936) reads `local_address()` once. When
330	  `served_is_current` is false it calls `remote::serving_certificate`
331	  with the Keychain key it already holds (:2951-2956), dispatches
332	  `ServedCertificateMade`, and builds `tls_config` from the updated
333	  identity. A failure is logged and the port serves
334	  `identity.certificate` as today.
335	- The core routes `ServedCertificateMade` with the other remote
336	  actions (`src/core/action.rs:1257`).
337	- In `SwitchboardApp::dispatch`, after an `AppAction::OpenPairing`, the
338	  app compares
339	  `local_address()` with `identity.served.address`. When they differ it
340	  calls `bind_remote` again, which reissues and rebinds; the QR is
341	  drawn from the new `served.address` on the next frame. Existing
342	  connections drop with the old listener, as a `SetRemoteListen`
343	  rebind does today. The address lookup goes through a field
344	  `address_source: fn() -> Option<IpAddr>` on `SwitchboardApp`,
345	  `remote::local_address` by default and set by a test-only
346	  `set_address_source`, beside `set_remote_port_override`
347	  (`src/app.rs:2920`).
348	
349	- `serve_remote` (:3017) routes `("GET", ["device"])` after
350	  `authenticate` to a new `remote_device`, which returns `{device_id,
351	  name, scope}` in the envelope.
352	- `authenticate` (:3127) checks `request.bearer` first, unchanged. Then
353	  it checks `request.cookie`. A cookie-authenticated request passes only
354	  when `origin` is absent or equals `https://{host}`, and either it is
355	  an upgrade whose `origin` equals `https://{host}`, or it carries
356	  `page`. Otherwise the reply is 403 `cross_origin`, "this request did
357	  not come from the host's page". The reasoning: a browser always sends
358	  `Origin` on a WebSocket handshake (RFC 6455 §4.1). A custom request
359	  header forces a CORS preflight, which the host never answers (Fetch
360	  standard). A same-origin GET in `cors` mode carries no `Origin`, so
361	  "absent" is accepted; `Origin: null` is not `https://{host}` and is
362	  refused. The tests prove the host's side of the rule only.
363	- `serve_remote` answers `GET /`, `/app.js` and `/app.css` that reached
364	  it (they carried a cookie) before the `/api/v1/` strip: the bytes,
365	  with `authenticated` set when `device_by_token` knows the cookie.
366	- `remote_pair` (:3606): when the body has `"cookie": true`, the
367	  request must carry `page`, else 403 `cross_origin`. The device is
368	  made with `Scope::Read` whatever the window's scope (decision 1):
369	  `new_device` (`src/core/remote.rs:166`) gains no parameter; the app
370	  sets `device.scope = Scope::Read` before dispatching `Paired`. The
371	  reply's `scope` says `read`, omits `token`, and sets
372	  `cookie: Some(token)`. Without `cookie` it is unchanged.
373	- `remote_info` (:3568) adds `"web"` to `capabilities`.
374	- The invite moves out of `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166` into a pure
375	  function in `src/core/remote.rs`: `pub fn invite_url(identity:
376	  &Identity, code: &str, port: u16) -> Option<String>`. The host is
377	  `identity.served`'s `address`, so the QR names exactly the address
378	  the served leaf carries; it returns `None` when there is none.
379	  `SocketAddr::new(address, port)`'s `Display` brackets IPv6.
380	
381	## The UI
382	
383	- **The pairing window** (`src/ui/remote.rs:141`) draws its QR from
384	  `invite_url`, so `remote::local_address()` leaves the dialog (:157)
385	  and the frame does no lookup. The QR cache is keyed by the URL, not
386	  the code (:168-172). "Copy invite" copies
387	  the URL. A new line under the code says: "Scan with a phone's camera
388	  to open the page in its browser. The browser warns that the
389	  certificate is not trusted. Accepting it on a network you trust is
390	  the trust step. The key in the code stops the page pairing with
391	  another host by mistake, not an impostor. A browser pairs read-only;
392	  raise it below once it is yours." The stale hover on Control (:218)
393	  becomes "Reads, and sending replies into a session. A browser still
394	  pairs read-only."
395	- **The devices list** (`src/ui/remote.rs:230-276`): the scope combo's
396	  hover says "Control lets this device type into sessions. For a
397	  browser, raise it only if you paired it yourself, just now, and saw
398	  no second certificate warning."
399	- **The page** (`web/`, plain JS, no framework):
400	  - **Load.** Read `location.hash`, call
401	    `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`, then `GET /api/v1/info`. If
402	    the fragment's `key` and `id` match `/info`, post `/pair` with
403	    `{code, spki_sha256: key, device_name, cookie: true}`; on a
404	    mismatch, say "This code is for another host" and post nothing.
405	    Keep `{server_id, spki_sha256}` in storage. Every `fetch` carries
406	    `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`.
407	  - **Header.** `server_name`, plus the device's name and scope from
408	    `/device`.
409	  - **Live data.** Open `wss://${location.host}/api/v1/events`. After
410	    `hello`, snapshot `projects`, each project's `sessions` and
411	    `waiting`. Apply buffered and later `changed` events by per-key
412	    revision as §4.4 says: refetch the resource the event names when
413	    its revision is past what the page holds. On `resync_required` or a
414	    close, reconnect and resync. Do the same on `visibilitychange` to
415	    visible (facts:47). If the socket fails before `hello`, poll the
416	    same reads every 5 s.
417	  - **The list.** Projects with a waiting session come first. Within a
418	    project, waiting sessions come first and are marked. Each row shows
419	    kind, liveness and the line from the departure above.
420	  - **The session view.** A Claude Code session shows `last-response`.
421	    A running session of any other kind shows `screen`, after a `watch`
422	    frame and its `watching` answer, and sends `unwatch` on leave.
423	    Refetch on the key's `changed` and every 30 s while visible, as
424	    §4.4 says. A stopped non-Claude session shows the note.
425	  - **Reply.** Shown only under `control`. It posts
426	    `sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, where `op` is 16 random
427	    bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` as hex. `randomUUID` needs a
428	    secure context, which facts list as Unresolved (facts:45). A `403
429	    scope` hides the box. Under `read`, where every browser starts, the
430	    box's place says "Read-only. Raise this device to Control in Remote
431	    devices on the Mac to reply." `/device` is reread on every socket
432	    `hello`, on `visibilitychange` and on a `403 scope`, so a raise shows
433	    without a re-pair.
434	  - **States.** "Not paired", "Revoked", "Identity changed, pair again"
435	    and "Pairing is closed" are each said in a sentence. Resume, Trust,
436	    drafts, tickets and the conversation beyond the last response stay
437	    out (the issue's Not in this cut).

442	  - `invite_url` for a served leaf with an IPv4 and an IPv6 address,

# Plan for #230: the browser page on the remote port

Worktree at 7fe8949. Line references are to this tree. `SCHEMA_VERSION`
is 16 (`src/core/model.rs:12`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1
(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). Neither moves: the one serialized change is
an additive `#[serde(default)]` field on `Identity`, the way `listen`
was added under version 1 (`src/ports/remote.rs:39-40`); see The
record. "Facts" is `facts/1/repo/facts.md`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **The code travels in the fragment, not the query.** The QR is
  `https://<addr>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
  A browser never sends a fragment to the server, so the code never
  reaches a request target, `RemoteRequest::query` or a `Referer`. It
  reaches the host only in the `/pair` body. That makes the notes'
  questions about logging the query, refusing a `GET /?code=`, and
  `Referer` leakage go away. This rests on RFC 3986 §3.5 (the user agent
  handles the fragment). That is not in the facts file, and
  `tests/remote.rs` cannot show it, because the host's client is not a
  browser. The page still calls `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`
  before anything else, but facts list whether Safari or the camera
  records the URL first as Unresolved (facts:46). The fragment does not
  change that, and the plan accepts it: the code is single-use, and the
  window closes on the first pairing (`src/core/remote.rs:64`).
- **The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire.** `agent_excerpt`
  derives it in the UI from the parsed conversation (facts:17,
  `src/ui/cards.rs:558-574`), and `SessionView` has no such field
  (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`). The page's list shows
  `waiting_reason` when the session is waiting, otherwise the card word
  (`card`), plus the first line of `notes`. Facts leave the excerpt to
  the owner (facts:83). If the owner wants it, the fallback is an
  additive `#[serde(default)] excerpt: Option<String>` on `SessionView`,
  computed on the host by the `agent_excerpt` rule. That means a
  fixture rewrite and a `revision.rs` fingerprint change, so it is a
  separate commit.
- **The current certificate is not one a phone is sure to accept.** It
  has no SAN, validity to 4096, and no serverAuth EKU (facts:13, :33).
  The host issues a second, served leaf over the same Keychain key,
  keeps it in `identity.json`, and reissues it only when its names no
  longer match or its expiry is within 30 days (details under The
  record and The signals). Pins survive (facts:12, spec §5 "a
  certificate reissued from the same key"). A browser's acceptance of
  the served leaf survives an app restart, because the leaf is the same
  bytes. Each issue has its own random serial, so no two certificates
  share issuer and serial (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.2; rcgen would otherwise
  derive the serial from the key, `rcgen-0.14.10/src/certificate.rs:458-468`).
- **"Revoked" is told apart by the page, not the host.** A revoked
  token and an unknown token get the same 401 (`src/app.rs:3142-3148`).
  The page keeps `{server_id, spki_sha256}` per origin in
  `localStorage`. On a 401 it says "revoked" when `/info` still shows
  that key, "identity changed, pair again" when the key differs, and
  "not paired" when it kept nothing. Facts leave this to the owner
  (facts:91). If the owner says otherwise, the fallback is a distinct
  401 code, which needs a record of revoked token hashes. Safari wipes
  script storage after 7 days without a visit (facts:32), so after that
  a revoked browser hears "not paired, scan the QR". That is still the
  right instruction.
- **"The screen for anything else" has no screen when the session is
  stopped.** `screen` refuses a session that is not running (spec
  §4.3). The page says "Not running; nothing to show". Facts leave this
  to the owner (facts:94). If the owner wants more, the fallback is
  `runs` then `runs/{n}/output` for a command or service.
- **The cookie is not scoped by port** (facts:28). A cookie set by
  `https://<ip>:43187` is sent to every port on that address. So the
  cookie name carries the port. Every cookie-authenticated request also
  passes an origin check, because `SameSite=Strict` does not stop
  another HTTPS service on the same IP: that service is same-site.

## Decisions

1. **Trust: the click-through is the trust step, and a browser pairs
   `read` only.** This is the owner's decision (facts:56-58), not a
   settled line, and it weakens two guarantees of §5:
   - "Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent"
     (`docs/remote-client.md:309`). A browser cannot. An impostor that
     the owner clicks through serves its own page, reads the fragment
     and relays the code with the real key. The URL's `key` then only
     catches a QR for another host or a stale QR: a genuine page
     compares it with `/info`'s self-reported `spki_sha256` and posts
     nothing on a mismatch.
   - "after pairing, every connection verifies the pin before the token
     is presented" (same line), and the token "is sent only as a bearer
     header over the pinned connection" (`:312`). A browser sends its
     cookie to whatever certificate it has accepted for the origin.

   What the plan builds against that: a stable served leaf (The
   record), so a second warning on a known origin is
   a sign of trouble rather than routine; and **a browser pairing is
   granted `read` whatever the window's scope.** The owner raises it to
   `control` by hand in the devices dialog, which §5 already allows
   (`docs/remote-client.md:314`). A relayed code therefore yields a
   reader, never a device that types into agent sessions, unless the
   owner raises it. The host tells a browser pairing by the `/pair`
   body's `"cookie": true` (decision 2). The dialog says what the
   click-through trusts in one sentence, and the hover on a browser's
   scope combo says what raising it trusts.

   §5's lines 309, 312 and 317 are rewritten to say the native
   guarantee and the browser's weaker one side by side, not added to
   (Docs).

   **If the owner rejects the click-through as the trust step**, the
   fallback the implementer builds is facts:58: the host serves its
   certificate before pairing at `GET /certificate`
   (`application/x-x509-ca-cert`), issued with basicConstraints CA:TRUE
   plus the served leaf's SAN, EKU and ≤825-day validity (facts:33,
   :34). The dialog gives the Settings > General > About > Certificate
   Trust Settings steps (facts:34), the pre-pairing rule names a fourth
   path, and browsers keep the window's scope. Without that answer the
   build is the read cap above.

   Separately, whether iOS Safari opens `wss://` after the click-through
   is Unresolved (facts:38, owner item facts:53). **The build does not
   depend on that answer.** The page falls back on its own to polling
   REST every 5 s when the socket fails before `hello`. Spike 23
   records it (Tests).
2. **Token: an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` cookie, no
   `Domain`, `Max-Age=34560000`.** The page's script never sees it. It
   survives Safari's 7-day storage cap where `localStorage` does not
   (facts:32). The same-origin WebSocket handshake sends it (facts:25).
   Name: `switchboard-<port>`, so two instances on one Mac never
   overwrite each other's cookie (facts:28). Native clients keep the
   bearer header, which is checked first. The page calls `fetch` in its
   default mode (`cors`) and never sets `mode` or `referrerPolicy` on a
   request: under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, a non-GET request in
   any other mode carries `Origin: null` (Fetch, "append a request
   `Origin` header" step 4.1), which the origin rule refuses. Whether a page reached through
   a certificate override is a secure context, and so keeps a `Secure`
   cookie, is Unresolved (facts:45). If Safari drops the cookie, the
   fallback is the subprotocol route: `/pair` returns the token in the
   body, the page keeps it in `localStorage`, sends it as
   `Authorization` on `fetch` and as the offered `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`,
   and `respond_upgrade` echoes it (facts:18, :26, :27). Re-pairing
   after 7 days unused is the known cost.
3. **One QR: the URL.** The JSON form leaves the QR and "Copy invite".
   `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
   accepts the URL and still accepts the JSON, because
   `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` lines and older pasted invites are JSON. That
   one function covers every caller (facts:14). The URL carries one
   address: the routed address the served leaf names
   (`ServedCertificate::address`, The record), bracketed when it is
   IPv6, so the QR's host and the certificate's SAN cannot disagree.
   When the pairing window opens and `local_address()` differs from
   that address (the Mac changed networks since the bind), the app
   reissues the leaf and rebinds before the QR is drawn (The actions
   and effects). The dialog already shows only one address. Facts leave which
   address to the owner (facts:71). If the owner says otherwise, the
   fallback is a `.local` name, which is Unresolved (facts:49) and not
   built.
4. **Static paths.** `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
   `GET /app.js` (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.css`
   (`text/css; charset=utf-8`). Nothing else: `/index.html`,
   `/favicon.ico` and every other non-API path answer 404 `not_found`
   as today. Each of the three carries `Content-Security-Policy:
   default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src
   'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none';
   frame-ancestors 'none'` as a header. `connect-src 'self'` covers the
   same-origin `wss:` (facts:30), and `frame-ancestors` must be a
   header (facts:31). They also carry `Cache-Control: no-store`,
   `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
   Every JSON reply also gains `Cache-Control: no-store` and `nosniff`.
   A static request **without** a `switchboard-<port>` cookie is
   answered by the connection thread, without the frame, the way it
   answers 429: the bytes are compile-time constants with nothing of
   the host in them. A static request **with** that cookie goes to the
   frame, which serves the same bytes and answers `authenticated: true`
   when the cookie is a known token (`device_by_token`, no
   `DeviceSeen`, no origin rule: a GET of public bytes has no effect).
   The connection then moves to the paired pool as an API request's
   does (`src/adapters/remote.rs:834-848`). Without this, a paired
   phone's reload leaves connections that fetched only `/app.css` in the
   unauthenticated pool for the 30 s idle timeout (`:573`, set at
   `:785`), and the accept loop drops a fifth (`:701-706`): the phone's
   own `/device` and anyone's `/info` would be locked out for 30 s. An
   unknown cookie still gets the page, unauthenticated. Facts leave the
   thread to the owner (facts:74); the fallback is answering every
   static request in `serve_remote` before the `/api/v1/` strip. Static
   loads count in a new `page` window of 60 a minute per listener,
   shared by the three paths. How many connections iOS Safari opens at
   once is Unresolved (facts:48). An unpaired load is three files and
   `/info`, so at most four in the stranger pool, each held up to 30 s
   idle. Spike 23 counts them; if an unpaired load or a pairing right
   after it is dropped, the fallback is `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` 4 → 8 and
   the §4.1 line with it. §5's rule becomes: before pairing,
   nothing but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's three files, which carry
   nothing of the host. With neither a fragment nor a cookie, the page
   shows `/info`'s `server_name`, whether pairing is open, and "On the
   Mac, open Remote devices, allow pairing and scan the QR" (the owner
   question at facts:77; the fallback is static text alone).
5. **Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/index.html`,
   `web/app.js` and `web/app.css` are embedded with `include_str!`
   (the precedent for embedding is `include_bytes!` at
   `src/main.rs:167`; the tree has no `include_str!` yet). The test checks a fixed list
   of referenced paths. There is no HTML parser (facts:21) and no JS
   test harness, since the page has no build step and no dependency.
6. **Device record.** The page sends `device_name` from
   `navigator.userAgent`: "Safari on iPhone", "Safari on Mac", "Chrome
   on Android", and so on, else "Browser". Safari on iPadOS sends the
   Mac user agent by default
   (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/119186), so a Mac user
   agent with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1` is named "Safari on iPad".
   A heuristic: a Mac with a touch screen would read as an iPad, and
   the owner sees the name only in the devices list.
   `/pair` already takes it (`src/app.rs:3650`) and caps it at 64
   characters (`src/core/remote.rs:166`). Scope is `read` for a browser
   whatever the window says (decision 1). The device is listed and revocable as any other. There is no
   `kind` field; the name tells devices apart. Facts leave this to the
   owner (facts:80). If the owner wants one, the fallback is an additive
   `#[serde(default)] kind` on `PairedDevice`, with no version
   (facts:16).
7. **The page's scope after a reload: `GET /api/v1/device`.** It
   answers `{device_id, name, scope}` under any scope. The page cannot
   do without it: the cookie is unreadable, and storage is wiped after
   7 days. It is also the request the page uses to learn it was
   revoked. Facts leave this to the owner (facts:87). If the owner says
   no, the fallback is to keep the scope from the `/pair` reply in
   `localStorage`, show the reply box when the scope is unknown, and
   hide it on a `403 scope`.
8. **The cookie reaches every endpoint the bearer does.** There is no
   second allowlist, because scope is the authority and a browser is a
   paired device like any other. Facts leave this to the owner
   (facts:65). If the owner says otherwise, the fallback is a match on
   how the request authenticated, limited to the page's paths.
9. **`/info` lists a `web` capability.** It is additive: the Swift
   client checks `capabilities.contains(..)` (for example
   `client/Sources/SwitchboardClientCore/ServerConnection.swift:431`),
   so an unknown word is ignored.

## The record

`devices.json`: no change. A browser is a `PairedDevice`; the token's
hash is the same whether the token travels as a bearer header or as a
cookie.

`identity.json` gains the served leaf, so a browser's acceptance
survives a restart. `Identity` (`src/ports/remote.rs:26`) gets an
additive `#[serde(default)] pub served: Option<ServedCertificate>`,
under `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged, as `listen` was
(`:39-40`). It is a field of the existing file rather than a new one
because it is written through the same `Effect::SaveIdentity` and
`RemoteStore::save_identity` path, so no port method is added.

```rust
/// The certificate the port serves: over the identity's key, naming
/// where a browser reaches the host. Reissued only when `names` or
/// `address` no longer match or `not_after` is near.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ServedCertificate {
    /// DER, base64.
    pub certificate: String,
    /// The SANs it carries, in order.
    pub names: Vec<String>,
    /// The routed address among them, which the QR uses.
    pub address: Option<IpAddr>,
    pub not_after: SystemTime,
}
```

`certificate` in `Identity` stays as it is (the identity's own record
and what `make_identity` checks against the key); `tls_config` serves
`served` when present. A key rotation makes a new identity with
`served: None`. An older build reads the file and ignores the field
(`Identity` has no `deny_unknown_fields`); if it saves the identity, the
field is dropped and the next newer launch issues a fresh leaf, which a
browser meets as one more warning. The struct literals of `Identity`
gain `served: None` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:117`,
`src/core/tests.rs:11769`, `tests/ui.rs:7436`).

Rehydration: at bind the app compares `served` with the names it would
issue now and its expiry; a match is served as it is, anything else is
reissued and saved (The actions and effects). Nothing else new is
rehydrated. A browser's only state is its cookie and the
`{server_id, spki_sha256}` it keeps in storage for that origin. A
change of the Mac's address is a new origin, so the browser pairs again
from a fresh QR. Write that under Known gaps.

  named `switchboard-<port>`; other cookies are dropped. `origin:

- `connection` (:770) answers the three static paths itself when the

- `respond` (:530) takes a content type and extra header lines.
  `RemoteReply` (:389) gains `cookie: Option<String>`, the token to set

- **The served leaf.** A new `pub fn serving_certificate(identity,
  key_pem, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime) ->
  Result<ServedCertificate, String>` makes the leaf over the Keychain
  key with `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem` (facts:12). It keeps the CN of
  `make_identity`. The SANs are `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the
  routed address; rcgen turns an IP string into `SanType::IpAddress`
  (facts:13). It sets `extended_key_usages = [ServerAuth]`,
  `not_before = now − 1 day`, `not_after = now + 800 days` (under
  Apple's 825, facts:33), and `serial_number =

  (`rcgen-0.14.10/src/lib.rs:878`). `time` is already in the tree at
  0.3.55 behind rcgen. Add it as a direct dependency (`time = "0.3"`)
  for `OffsetDateTime::from(SystemTime)`, and commit the updated
  `Cargo.lock`.
- `tls_config` (:144) serves `identity.served` when it is present and
  `identity.certificate` otherwise. Its signature does not change.
- The rule for when to reissue is a pure function in
  `src/core/remote.rs`: `pub fn served_is_current(served:
  Option<&ServedCertificate>, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime)
  -> bool`, true when `served` exists, names `address`, and expires more
  than 30 days after `now`. If the owner answers "no" on naming the IP
  (facts:59), the SANs drop the routed address and `address` is not
  compared; the QR then takes `local_address()` itself.

## The actions and effects

One new action, `AppAction::ServedCertificateMade(ServedCertificate)`:
the core stores it on the identity through `update_identity`
(`src/core/remote.rs:105`), which emits the existing
`Effect::SaveIdentity`. No new `Effect`. `Paired` and `RevokeDevice`
carry a browser unchanged. The frame changes in `src/app.rs`:

- `bind_remote` (:2936) reads `local_address()` once. When
  `served_is_current` is false it calls `remote::serving_certificate`
  with the Keychain key it already holds (:2951-2956), dispatches
  `ServedCertificateMade`, and builds `tls_config` from the updated
  identity. A failure is logged and the port serves
  `identity.certificate` as today.
- The core routes `ServedCertificateMade` with the other remote
  actions (`src/core/action.rs:1257`).
- In `SwitchboardApp::dispatch`, after an `AppAction::OpenPairing`, the
  app compares
  `local_address()` with `identity.served.address`. When they differ it
  calls `bind_remote` again, which reissues and rebinds; the QR is
  drawn from the new `served.address` on the next frame. Existing
  connections drop with the old listener, as a `SetRemoteListen`
  rebind does today. The address lookup goes through a field
  `address_source: fn() -> Option<IpAddr>` on `SwitchboardApp`,
  `remote::local_address` by default and set by a test-only
  `set_address_source`, beside `set_remote_port_override`
  (`src/app.rs:2920`).

- `serve_remote` (:3017) routes `("GET", ["device"])` after
  `authenticate` to a new `remote_device`, which returns `{device_id,
  name, scope}` in the envelope.
- `authenticate` (:3127) checks `request.bearer` first, unchanged. Then
  it checks `request.cookie`. A cookie-authenticated request passes only
  when `origin` is absent or equals `https://{host}`, and either it is
  an upgrade whose `origin` equals `https://{host}`, or it carries
  `page`. Otherwise the reply is 403 `cross_origin`, "this request did
  not come from the host's page". The reasoning: a browser always sends
  `Origin` on a WebSocket handshake (RFC 6455 §4.1). A custom request
  header forces a CORS preflight, which the host never answers (Fetch
  standard). A same-origin GET in `cors` mode carries no `Origin`, so
  "absent" is accepted; `Origin: null` is not `https://{host}` and is
  refused. The tests prove the host's side of the rule only.
- `serve_remote` answers `GET /`, `/app.js` and `/app.css` that reached
  it (they carried a cookie) before the `/api/v1/` strip: the bytes,
  with `authenticated` set when `device_by_token` knows the cookie.
- `remote_pair` (:3606): when the body has `"cookie": true`, the
  request must carry `page`, else 403 `cross_origin`. The device is
  made with `Scope::Read` whatever the window's scope (decision 1):
  `new_device` (`src/core/remote.rs:166`) gains no parameter; the app
  sets `device.scope = Scope::Read` before dispatching `Paired`. The
  reply's `scope` says `read`, omits `token`, and sets
  `cookie: Some(token)`. Without `cookie` it is unchanged.
- `remote_info` (:3568) adds `"web"` to `capabilities`.
- The invite moves out of `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166` into a pure
  function in `src/core/remote.rs`: `pub fn invite_url(identity:
  &Identity, code: &str, port: u16) -> Option<String>`. The host is
  `identity.served`'s `address`, so the QR names exactly the address
  the served leaf carries; it returns `None` when there is none.
  `SocketAddr::new(address, port)`'s `Display` brackets IPv6.

## The UI

- **The pairing window** (`src/ui/remote.rs:141`) draws its QR from
  `invite_url`, so `remote::local_address()` leaves the dialog (:157)
  and the frame does no lookup. The QR cache is keyed by the URL, not
  the code (:168-172). "Copy invite" copies
  the URL. A new line under the code says: "Scan with a phone's camera
  to open the page in its browser. The browser warns that the
  certificate is not trusted. Accepting it on a network you trust is
  the trust step. The key in the code stops the page pairing with
  another host by mistake, not an impostor. A browser pairs read-only;
  raise it below once it is yours." The stale hover on Control (:218)
  becomes "Reads, and sending replies into a session. A browser still
  pairs read-only."
- **The devices list** (`src/ui/remote.rs:230-276`): the scope combo's
  hover says "Control lets this device type into sessions. For a
  browser, raise it only if you paired it yourself, just now, and saw
  no second certificate warning."
- **The page** (`web/`, plain JS, no framework):
  - **Load.** Read `location.hash`, call
    `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`, then `GET /api/v1/info`. If
    the fragment's `key` and `id` match `/info`, post `/pair` with
    `{code, spki_sha256: key, device_name, cookie: true}`; on a
    mismatch, say "This code is for another host" and post nothing.
    Keep `{server_id, spki_sha256}` in storage. Every `fetch` carries
    `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`.
  - **Header.** `server_name`, plus the device's name and scope from
    `/device`.
  - **Live data.** Open `wss://${location.host}/api/v1/events`. After
    `hello`, snapshot `projects`, each project's `sessions` and
    `waiting`. Apply buffered and later `changed` events by per-key
    revision as §4.4 says: refetch the resource the event names when
    its revision is past what the page holds. On `resync_required` or a
    close, reconnect and resync. Do the same on `visibilitychange` to
    visible (facts:47). If the socket fails before `hello`, poll the
    same reads every 5 s.
  - **The list.** Projects with a waiting session come first. Within a
    project, waiting sessions come first and are marked. Each row shows
    kind, liveness and the line from the departure above.
  - **The session view.** A Claude Code session shows `last-response`.
    A running session of any other kind shows `screen`, after a `watch`
    frame and its `watching` answer, and sends `unwatch` on leave.
    Refetch on the key's `changed` and every 30 s while visible, as
    §4.4 says. A stopped non-Claude session shows the note.
  - **Reply.** Shown only under `control`. It posts
    `sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, where `op` is 16 random
    bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` as hex. `randomUUID` needs a
    secure context, which facts list as Unresolved (facts:45). A `403
    scope` hides the box. Under `read`, where every browser starts, the
    box's place says "Read-only. Raise this device to Control in Remote
    devices on the Mac to reply." `/device` is reread on every socket
    `hello`, on `visibilitychange` and on a `403 scope`, so a raise shows
    without a re-pair.
  - **States.** "Not paired", "Revoked", "Identity changed, pair again"
    and "Pairing is closed" are each said in a sentence. Resume, Trust,
    drafts, tickets and the conversation beyond the last response stay
    out (the issue's Not in this cut).

- **Test.** The cookie test checks that `Origin: null` on `/device` and

# Feedback on the plan for #230, round 2

## Earlier points

1. Settled. The plan adds a random serial, a persisted served leaf under an additive `#[serde(default)]` field, the reissue rule, and the spike's relaunch check.
2. Settled. The plan states the weakening of §5 as the owner's decision, caps a browser pairing at `read`, writes the download fallback, and rewrites §5 lines 309, 312 and 317.
3. Settled. The QR's host now comes from `served.address`, and the app rebinds after `OpenPairing` when the address has moved, with a test for both.
4. Settled. A Mac user agent with `maxTouchPoints > 1` is named "Safari on iPad", and the plan says the heuristic misnames a touch-screen Mac.
5. Settled. The page uses `fetch`'s default mode, `Origin: null` is refused, and a test covers it.
6. Settled. A static request with a cookie goes to the frame and moves its connection to the paired pool, with a pool test. The accept-loop citation in decision 4 should read `:701-705`.
7. Settled.

## Cuts

### Decisions

- **Decision 4: two ways to serve the same three files.** The page is served on the connection thread when the request has no cookie and through the frame when it has one. Since the frame has to serve them anyway, serve all three in `serve_remote`. That is already the plan's written fallback. It removes the `cookie`-dependent branch in `connection` and the "without/with a cookie" paragraph. The new `page` rate window still bounds the frame's load, three files per unpaired visit against 8 drains per pass.
- **Decision 9 and the `web` capability:** cut. No client reads it. The Swift client doesn't, and the page doesn't need to ask its own host. Remove it from decision 9, `remote_info`, the `info_is_served_to_anyone…` test change, and Contract additions.

### The record

- **`ServedCertificate::names`:** cut. Nothing reads it. `served_is_current` compares only `address` and `not_after`, and the SANs other than the address are fixed constants. Drop the field and the doc comment's "`names` or".
- **The list of `Identity` struct literals that gain `served: None`** (`src/adapters/remote.rs:117`, `src/core/tests.rs:11769`, `tests/ui.rs:7436`): cut. The compiler forces each one.
- **The "Rehydration" paragraph:** cut. It restates the `bind_remote` bullet under The actions and effects. Keep only the Known-gaps sentence about a changed address.

### The signals

input.old_string:
A static request **without** a `switchboard-<port>` cookie is
   answered by the connection thread, without the frame, the way it
   answers 429: the bytes are compile-time constants with nothing of
   the host in them. A static request **with** that cookie goes to the
   frame, which serves the same bytes and answers `authenticated: true`
   when the cookie is a known token (`device_by_token`, no
   `DeviceSeen`, no origin rule: a GET of public bytes has no effect).
   The connection then moves to the paired pool as an API request's
   does (`src/adapters/remote.rs:834-848`). Without this, a paired
   phone's reload leaves connections that fetched only `/app.css` in the
   unauthenticated pool for the 30 s idle timeout (`:573`, set at
   `:785`), and the accept loop drops a fifth (`:701-706`): the phone's
   own `/device` and anyone's `/info` would be locked out for 30 s. An
   unknown cookie still gets the page, unauthenticated. Facts leave the
   thread to the owner (facts:74); the fallback is answering every
   static request in `serve_remote` before the `/api/v1/` strip. Static
   loads count in a new `page` window of 60 a minute per listener,
   shared by the three paths.
input.new_string:
`serve_remote` answers all three on the frame, before the `/api/v1/`
   strip. When the request carries a `switchboard-<port>` cookie that
   `device_by_token` knows, the answer is `authenticated: true` (no
   `DeviceSeen`, no origin rule: a GET of public bytes has no effect),
   so the connection moves to the paired pool as an API request's does
   (`src/adapters/remote.rs:835-848`). Otherwise a paired phone's
   reload would leave connections that fetched only `/app.css` in the
   unauthenticated pool for the 30 s idle timeout (`:573`, set at
   `:785`), and the accept loop drops a fifth (`:701-705`): the phone's
   own `/device` and anyone's `/info` would be locked out for 30 s. An
   unknown or absent cookie still gets the page, unauthenticated. Facts
   leave the thread to the owner (facts:74); the frame is chosen
   because it has to serve the cookie case anyway, and one path is
   simpler than two. Static loads count in a new `page` window of 60 a
   minute per listener, shared by the three paths and checked on the
   connection thread with the others, which bounds the frame's load:
   three files per unpaired visit against 8 drains per pass.

244	pub struct ServedCertificate {
245	    /// DER, base64.
246	    pub certificate: String,
247	    /// The routed address among its SANs, which the QR uses.
248	    pub address: Option<IpAddr>,
249	    pub not_after: SystemTime,

307	## The actions and effects
308	
309	One new action, `AppAction::ServedCertificateMade(ServedCertificate)`:
310	the core stores it on the identity through `update_identity`

316	  `served_is_current` is false it calls `remote::serving_certificate`

322	  actions (`src/core/action.rs:1257`).

326	  calls `bind_remote` again, which reissues and rebinds; the QR is
327	  drawn from the new `served.address` on the next frame. Existing
328	  connections drop with the old listener, as a `SetRemoteListen`

358	  `cookie: Some(token)`. Without `cookie` it is unchanged.

362	  `identity.served`'s `address`, so the QR names exactly the address
363	  the served leaf carries; it returns `None` when there is none.

   after it is dropped, the fallback is `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` 4 → 8 and
   the §4.1 line with it. §5's rule becomes: before pairing,
   nothing but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's three files, which carry
   nothing of the host. With neither a fragment nor a cookie, the page
   shows `/info`'s `server_name`, whether pairing is open, and "On the
   Mac, open Remote devices, allow pairing and scan the QR" (the owner
   question at facts:77; the fallback is static text alone).

   `web/app.js` and `web/app.css` are embedded with `include_str!`
   (the precedent for embedding is `include_bytes!` at
   `src/main.rs:167`; the tree has no `include_str!` yet). The test checks a fixed list

   test harness, since the page has no build step and no dependency.

   `navigator.userAgent`: "Safari on iPhone", "Safari on Mac", "Chrome
   on Android", and so on, else "Browser". Safari on iPadOS sends the
   Mac user agent by default

   agent with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1` is named "Safari on iPad".

   the owner sees the name only in the devices list.

   characters (`src/core/remote.rs:166`). Scope is `read` for a browser
   whatever the window says (decision 1). The device is listed and revocable as any other. There is no

   owner (facts:80). If the owner wants one, the fallback is an additive
   `#[serde(default)] kind` on `PairedDevice`, with no version
   (facts:16).

   answers `{device_id, name, scope}` under any scope. The page cannot
   do without it: the cookie is unreadable, and storage is wiped after
   7 days. It is also the request the page uses to learn it was
   revoked. Facts leave this to the owner (facts:87). If the owner says
   no, the fallback is to keep the scope from the `/pair` reply in
   `localStorage`, show the reply box when the scope is unknown, and
   hide it on a `403 scope`.
8. **The cookie reaches every endpoint the bearer does.** There is no
   second allowlist, because scope is the authority and a browser is a
   paired device like any other. Facts leave this to the owner
   (facts:65). If the owner says otherwise, the fallback is a match on
   how the request authenticated, limited to the page's paths.

`devices.json`: no change. A browser is a `PairedDevice`; the token's
hash is the same whether the token travels as a bearer header or as a
cookie.

`identity.json` gains the served leaf, so a browser's acceptance
survives a restart. `Identity` (`src/ports/remote.rs:26`) gets an
additive `#[serde(default)] pub served: Option<ServedCertificate>`,
under `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged, as `listen` was
(`:39-40`). It is a field of the existing file rather than a new one
because it is written through the same `Effect::SaveIdentity` and
`RemoteStore::save_identity` path, so no port method is added.

```rust
/// The certificate the port serves: over the identity's key, naming
/// where a browser reaches the host. Reissued only when `address` no
/// longer matches or `not_after` is near.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ServedCertificate {
    /// DER, base64.
    pub certificate: String,
    /// The routed address among its SANs, which the QR uses.
    pub address: Option<IpAddr>,
    pub not_after: SystemTime,
}
```

`certificate` in `Identity` stays as it is (the identity's own record
and what `make_identity` checks against the key); `tls_config` serves
`served` when present. A key rotation makes a new identity with
`served: None`. An older build reads the file and ignores the field
(`Identity` has no `deny_unknown_fields`); if it saves the identity, the
field is dropped and the next newer launch issues a fresh leaf, which a
browser meets as one more warning.

A change of the Mac's address is a new origin, so the browser pairs
again from a fresh QR. Write that under Known gaps.

These change in `src/adapters/remote.rs`.

- `read_request` (:444) keeps three more headers on `RemoteRequest`
  (:360). `cookie: Option<String>` is only the value of the cookie
  named `switchboard-<port>`; other cookies are dropped. `origin:
  Option<String>` and `host: Option<String>` are the raw values.
  `page: bool` is true when `X-Switchboard-Page: 1` is present. The
  adapter learns its port from `Shared`, which gains `port: u16`,
  filled from `listener.local_addr()` in `bind` (:673).
- `Limits::limited` (:629) gains the `page` window for `/`, `/app.js`
  and `/app.css`; `connection` (:770) otherwise hands them to the frame
  like any request (decision 4).
- `respond` (:530) takes a content type and extra header lines.
  `RemoteReply` (:389) gains `cookie: Option<String>`, the token to set
  as `Set-Cookie`, and `content_type: &'static str`, so the frame's
  static answers carry their own type and headers.

  key_pem, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime) ->
  Result<ServedCertificate, String>` makes the leaf over the Keychain
  key with `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem` (facts:12). It keeps the CN of
  `make_identity`. The SANs are `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the
  routed address; rcgen turns an IP string into `SanType::IpAddress`
  (facts:13). It sets `extended_key_usages = [ServerAuth]`,
  `not_before = now − 1 day`, `not_after = now + 800 days` (under
  Apple's 825, facts:33), and `serial_number =
  Some(SerialNumber::from_slice(&r))` with `r` 16 bytes from
  `fill_random` and the top bit cleared so the integer is positive
  (`rcgen-0.14.10/src/lib.rs:878`). `time` is already in the tree at
  0.3.55 behind rcgen. Add it as a direct dependency (`time = "0.3"`)
  for `OffsetDateTime::from(SystemTime)`, and commit the updated
  `Cargo.lock`.

  `identity.certificate` otherwise. Its signature does not change.

  `src/core/remote.rs`: `pub fn served_is_current(served:
  Option<&ServedCertificate>, address: Option<IpAddr>, now: SystemTime)
  -> bool`, true when `served` exists, names `address`, and expires more
  than 30 days after `now`. If the owner answers "no" on naming the IP
  (facts:59), the SANs drop the routed address and `address` is not
  compared; the QR then takes `local_address()` itself.

the core stores it on the identity through `update_identity`

carry a browser unchanged. The frame changes in `src/app.rs`:

- `bind_remote` (:2936) reads `local_address()` once. When
  `served_is_current` is false it calls `remote::serving_certificate`
  with the Keychain key it already holds (:2951-2956), dispatches
  `ServedCertificateMade`, and builds `tls_config` from the updated
  identity. A failure is logged and the port serves
  `identity.certificate` as today.
- The core routes `ServedCertificateMade` with the other remote
  actions (`src/core/action.rs:1257`).
- In `SwitchboardApp::dispatch`, after an `AppAction::OpenPairing`, the
  app compares
  `local_address()` with `identity.served.address`. When they differ it
  calls `bind_remote` again, which reissues and rebinds; the QR is
  drawn from the new `served.address` on the next frame. Existing
  connections drop with the old listener, as a `SetRemoteListen`
  rebind does today. The address lookup goes through a field
  `address_source: fn() -> Option<IpAddr>` on `SwitchboardApp`,
  `remote::local_address` by default and set by a test-only
  `set_address_source`, beside `set_remote_port_override`

  name, scope}` in the envelope.

  an upgrade whose `origin` equals `https://{host}`, or it carries

  certificate is not trusted. Accepting it on a network you trust is
  the trust step. The key in the code stops the page pairing with
  another host by mistake, not an impostor. A browser pairs read-only;
  raise it below once it is yours." The stale hover on Control (:218)

  pairs read-only."

    mismatch, say "This code is for another host" and post nothing.

    `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`.

    visible (facts:47). If the socket fails before `hello`, poll the

    kind, liveness and the line from the departure above.
  - **The session view.** A Claude Code session shows `last-response`.
